lede.headline: Musk weighs merging Tesla and SpaceX after big earnings
lede.dek: A day after SpaceX posted a $4.4 billion profit, Musk said both boards have formed committees to explore combining it with Tesla, even as Tesla's own profit fell.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: Tesla profit falls as Musk weighs SpaceX merger
stories.move: Tesla's Q3 net income fell 44% to $787 million as revenue stayed flat at $28.05 billion and spending on Optimus and AI rose; free cash flow turned positive at $1.53 billion. A day earlier, SpaceX reported revenue up 161% to $14.6 billion and net income of $4.4 billion, and Musk said on SpaceX's earnings call that both companies have formed special board committees to explore merging them, which would need a majority vote of all Tesla shares.
stories.why: A combined company could let Musk's businesses share AI, chip and robotics work, and investors have started pricing in that possibility.
stories.bear: Musk said the committees haven't agreed on terms and a deal isn't guaranteed; Tesla's own numbers show a core auto business that is shrinking.
stories.watch: Tesla must hold its annual meeting by Dec 6, 2026, a possible venue for a shareholder vote on a merger.

stories.headline: Carlos Slim's firm sells $86 million of Talos Energy
stories.move: Control Empresarial de Capitales, Carlos Slim's holding company, sold about 4.9 million shares of Talos Energy between Oct 15 and Oct 19 for roughly $85.9 million combined, according to SEC filings. The sales cut its stake to 24.5 million shares, or 14.7% of the oil and gas company, from about 29.4 million shares.
stories.why: Slim's firm has been a major Talos shareholder for years; a steady reduction can signal he is reallocating away from the stock.
stories.bear: The filings don't say why the sales happened, and Slim's firm still owns a large, double-digit stake in the company.
stories.watch: Future SEC filings from Control Empresarial de Capitales for further changes to its Talos Energy stake.

stories.headline: Meta creates new stock class to keep Zuckerberg in California
stories.move: Meta's board created a new non-voting Class C stock, paying one Class C share for every Class A or Class B share starting January 2027, according to an SEC filing. Zuckerberg can freely sell 20% of the Class C shares he receives; the rest unlocks gradually over eight years. In exchange, he committed to remain a California resident, or wherever Meta is headquartered, for eight years.
stories.why: Zuckerberg had told Meta he was weighing a move out of California over its proposed billionaire tax; selling voting shares to cover a tax bill would have cut his control of the company.
stories.bear: The arrangement dilutes other shareholders with a new stock class, and the tax it is designed for, Proposition 40, hasn't passed yet.

stories.headline: Sergey Brin spends over $100 million fighting California tax
stories.move: Google co-founder Sergey Brin has put more than $100 million into Building a Better California, a group opposing Proposition 40, the state's proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires' net worth. Voters decide the measure on Nov 3, 2026.
stories.why: Brin is one of several wealthy Californians bankrolling the opposition; estimates suggest his own tax bill could run into the billions if it passes.
stories.bear: Supporters of the measure, including several Nobel-winning economists, say it would raise billions for the state and argue opponents are overstating the risk of billionaires leaving.

stories.headline: Ambani's Jio Platforms IPO fully subscribed within two hours
stories.move: Jio Platforms, Reliance Industries' telecom unit, drew enough bids to cover its entire $3.2 billion IPO within two hours of opening on Oct 21, according to BSE exchange data. The offer covers 197.5 million shares priced between 1,065 and 1,119 rupees each; Jio is expected to list on Oct 28.
stories.why: Strong demand suggests investors are betting on Jio's roughly 533 million subscribers despite a recent public dispute between Ambani and Elon Musk over Starlink's delayed India launch.
stories.bear: Reliance's own shares are down 23% this year, and some reports say the IPO's valuation is below earlier expectations.
stories.watch: Oct 28, 2026: expected Jio Platforms listing date in Mumbai.

stories.headline: Oracle's AI debt faces a stress test as bonds wobble
stories.move: Oracle's credit default swaps, a gauge of how risky bond investors see the company, have swung sharply over the past week. The company's S&P credit rating sits at BBB-, the lowest investment-grade level, after a July downgrade, and Oracle has issued $118 billion in long-term debt to help fund its AI data center buildout, including a large commitment tied to OpenAI.
stories.why: Investors are worried Oracle is borrowing heavily to fund AI data centers just as a competitor, CoreWeave, showed signs of debt stress this month.
stories.bear: Oracle says it remains focused on disciplined capital allocation and preserving its investment-grade rating, and some analysts say they aren't concerned about its debt levels.
stories.watch: Whether S&P or other raters cut Oracle's rating further toward junk.

stories.headline: Blue Origin plans new Florida launch pads for New Glenn
stories.move: Blue Origin announced plans on Oct 16 for two more launch pads at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, on top of two already under construction, aiming to support multiple New Glenn flights a week by the end of the decade. The company is also building a $330 million upper-stage factory at Rocket Park, targeted for mid-2027, and adding two more recovery ships.
stories.why: Blue Origin is racing to scale up launches after a May explosion damaged one of its pads, and wants more capacity before New Glenn returns to flight.
stories.bear: Neither new pad is built yet, the company is approved for only 12 launches a year while it has requested 50, and a federal environmental review is still underway.
stories.watch: Blue Origin says its New Glenn rocket is expected to return to flight in December 2026.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang says AI boom's bottleneck is now capital
stories.move: Speaking to CNBC at GTC Berlin on Oct 22, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said demand from 'neocloud' data-center operators is 'off the charts' but that funding, not customers, is now the constraint. He said Nvidia wants to establish its compute as a 'financeable asset' that lenders can treat as collateral, building on a $500 billion AI financing plan Nvidia announced in August with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR. Nvidia shares fell as much as 2% in premarket trading that day, and neocloud peers Nebius, IREN and Applied Digital all fell further.
stories.why: If Huang is right that financing, not demand, is the bottleneck, it suggests the AI buildout could keep going as long as lenders keep extending credit.
stories.bear: Bond investors have already pushed up borrowing costs for AI-heavy companies like CoreWeave and Oracle, and two banks have issued negative notes on CoreWeave this week.
stories.watch: Whether more lenders agree to treat AI compute as loan collateral.

quickHits: Dell shares rose 5.3% on Oct 21 after rival Super Micro raised its first-quarter revenue forecast to $18.5–$19.5 billion from $14.5–$15.5 billion, and after Dell announced new AI server hardware with Nvidia at GTC Berlin.
Google co-founder Larry Page bought two Miami homes for about $173 million and shifted his family office to Florida as California's wealth-tax vote nears.
Interactive Brokers began a limited rollout of autonomous AI trading to about 3,000 clients, founder Thomas Peterffy said on the firm's Q3 earnings call.
memo: Lenders and credit raters are scrutinizing AI spending as closely as the technology itself: Oracle's selloff was about its debt load, not its cloud growth.
A company can redesign its ownership structure quickly when a founder's incentives are at risk, as Meta just did for Zuckerberg.
A rival's updated outlook can move your stock overnight: Dell jumped partly because Super Micro raised its guidance, not because of its own news.

movers.why: SpaceX rose 7.8% after Q3 profit reached $4.4 billion and Musk called a Tesla merger a good idea.
